title: Fipa Acl Heritage
motto: Before MCP, before A2A, there was FIPA-ACL. In 2000 the IEEE Foundation for Intelligent Physical Agents ratified an agent communication language with twenty performatives, two content languages, and a set of interaction protocols — contract net, subscribe/notify, request-when. It faded from industry because the ontology overhead was too heavy for the web, but the LLM revival of multi-agent systems is quietly reimplementing the same ideas without the formal semantics: JSON contracts stand in for performatives, natural language stands in for ontologies. This lesson reads FIPA-ACL seriously so you can see which 2026 protocol decisions are reinvention, which are novelty, and where the current wave is going to rediscover problems the 2000s already solved.
